item.title: [UPDATED] Set up iPhone Handoff
item.description:
iPhone Handoff lets you use one phone number between two devices, so you can switch between them whenever you want. It makes it easy to move back and forth between devices optimized for the moment — like weekday business or weekend adventures.

4 added · 2 removed

-To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff. To stay in control of which iPhone is active, keep a passcode enabled on your iPhone and keep it private.
+To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The iPhone that you switched from will display an arrow icon at the top of your screen. +[Image: Two iPhones illustrating Handoff: the previously active iPhone shows an arrow icon, and the newly active iPhone displays "Switched to this iPhone" at the top of the screen.]

item.title: [UPDATED] Discover accessibility features for Apple Education
item.description:
With built-in speech, vision, mobility, hearing, and cognitive features, Apple devices provide students, teachers, and leaders with personalization they need to learn, create, thrive, and define their own success.

181 added · 113 removed

-At Apple, we believe that technology is most powerful when it empowers everyone. That's why for more than forty years, Apple has worked with educators to define the role of accessible technology in learning.
-
-In 1978, Apple introduced personal computers to the classroom. Apple established the Office of Special Education Programs, the industry's first disability solutions group, in 1985. And in 1987, we partnered with disability advocacy groups to found the Alliance for Technology Access to share expertise and advance accessibility nationwide in the United States, and our commitment to work closely with advocacy groups globally continues to this day.
-
-Today, Apple continues to support the diverse needs of every learner with powerful, built-in assistive features to create, communicate, personalize, build confidence, and achieve independence.
+At Apple, we believe that technology is most powerful when it empowers everyone. That's why for more than forty years, Apple has worked with educators to define the role of accessible technology in learning, beginning with the introduction of computers to classrooms in 1978, establishing the Office of Special Education Programs—the industry's first disability solutions group—in 1985, and co-founding the Alliance for Technology Access in 1987 to share expertise and advance accessibility in education.
+
+Apple continues to support the diverse needs of every learner with powerful, built-in assistive features that help students create, communicate, learn, build confidence, and achieve independence. 1 And with Apple Intelligence woven throughout, those features are more capable, more personal, and more responsive to each student’s needs than ever before. 2
-With built-in speech, vision, mobility, hearing, and cognitive features, customized learning tools, and alternative communication methods, students can engage with content in ways that resonate with their unique learning styles.
+With built-in accessibility features, customizable learning and writing tools, and alternative communication methods, Apple devices help students engage with content in ways that resonate with their unique learning styles.
-Apple devices help bring intentional, natural, and age-appropriate learning to life for early learners. To support emerging readers, Read & Speak features like Speak Screen and Speak Selection reads text aloud to students. 1 To help them stay focused and on track, Guided Access can limit a device to a single app.
+Apple's accessibility features support early learners—including children just beginning their educational journey, students who are neurodivergent or who have developmental or physical disabilities—by removing barriers to interaction and tailoring the digital experience to how young minds naturally learn. Read & Speak features like Speak Screen and Speak Selection support emerging readers by reading text aloud to students. Guided Access helps minimize wandering taps and distractions, limiting a device to a single app to keep young learners in the experience their teachers intended.
-To support multilingual learners, Apple devices provide features to customize language. Students can use Read & Speak to hear their writing out loud in eight distinct voices, with support for more than sixty languages and locales. 1 Live Captions display spoken words as text in real time, improving clarity and participation for learners. 2 Translate app lets students quickly and easily translate their voice and text between languages. 3 When viewing a webpage or image that's in another language, Safari can translate the text. 4
+To support multilingual learners, Apple devices offer robust language customization. Students can use Read & Speak to hear their writing aloud in 80 distinct voices, with support for over 60 languages and locales. Live Captions provide real-time, on-device transcriptions of conversations, enhancing clarity and participation for learners. 3 The Translate app enables quick and easy translation of voice and text between languages, while Safari automatically translates text when viewing webpages or images in another language.
-Apple devices are inclusive by design, with built-in accessibility features for vision, hearing, speech, mobility, and cognitive accessibility.
+Apple devices are designed to be inclusive, with built-in accessibility features for vision, hearing, speech, mobility, and cognitive needs.
-Vision features help students do more on their devices by adjusting what they see and how they interact, no matter their level of vision.
-
-#### Read & Speak
-
-Read & Speak is a collection of features designed to enhance a student's reading or writing experience with audio in over 80 distinct voices and more than 60 languages and locales. 1 Use Speak Screen to have the entire screen read aloud, or use Speak Selection to have a specific range of text read. Accessibility Reader gives students new ways to customize long-form text and focus on content they want to read, with extensive options for font, color, and spacing, as well as support for Spoken Content.
+Vision features help students who are blind or have low vision do more on their devices by enabling them to navigate their surroundings, control their devices, or customize their display.
+
+[Learn more about Apple vision features](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/vision/)
+
+#### VoiceOver
+
+VoiceOver describes what's onscreen—audibly, in braille, or both—enabling easy control and screen navigation through simple gestures on a touchscreen, trackpad, or Bluetooth keyboard. Students can type in braille directly on the touchscreen with Braille Screen Input. And with Live Recognition, 4 students get descriptions of objects in the real world, such as people, doors, text, and furniture in indoor spaces. 5 Image Explorer uses Apple Intelligence to give richer descriptions of images on screen, including complex visual materials like photographs and diagrams in assignments, scanned handouts, school forms, and personal records. Students can even ask follow-up questions in their own words to get more visual information.
+
+[Learn more about VoiceOver](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/#modal-vision_voiceover)
-Magnifier is a digital magnifying glass that zooms in on, detects, and describes physical objects. Format text within the camera's frame for easier reading, or speak text aloud, like words in a text book or on a whiteboard. Students who are blind or low vision can use Magnifier's Detection Mode to identify people, doors, furniture, and text within the frame. 5
+Magnifier works like a digital magnifying glass to detect, zoom in on, and describe physical objects. Learners can format text within the frame for easier reading, read textbook or whiteboard words aloud, or use Apple Intelligence for detailed visual descriptions, answers to follow-up questions, and voice controls like "zoom in" or "turn on flashlight." Detection Mode uses on-device machine learning to scan surroundings, with LiDAR-equipped iPads providing spatial feedback for detecting nearby people, doors, and furniture. 5 On Mac, Magnifier connects to an external camera to zoom in on surroundings—such as a screen, a whiteboard, or a printed worksheet—while multiple live session windows let students multitask between viewing a presentation and a book using Desk View. These views can be captured, grouped, and saved to return to later.
+
+[Learn more about Magnifier](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/#modal-vision_magnifier)
+
+#### Braille Access
+
+Braille Access is a braille-first experience that turns iPad or Mac into a fully integrated braille notetaker. With a built-in app launcher, students can open apps via connected braille devices, access Braille Ready Format (BRF) files, take notes in braille format, and perform calculations using Nemeth Braille or UEB Math, two codes often used in classrooms for math and science. Integrated Live Captions enable students and teachers to transcribe conversations in real time on braille displays, while Apple Intelligence generates summaries to help students who read braille at a slower pace follow along without missing the thread of a lesson or conversation. 3
+
+[Learn more about Braille Access](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/#modal-vision_braille-access)
+
+#### Read & Speak settings
+
+Read & Speak is a collection of features that enhances a student's reading and writing with audio, powered by over 80 voices across 60-plus languages and locales. Learners can have entire screens or selected text read aloud, with automatic language detection ensuring smooth voice transitions. Speech Controller keeps playback controls handy for pausing or adjusting speed, while Highlight Content accentuates words as they are spoken. These features integrate with Accessibility Reader, allowing students to customize fonts, colors, and spacing and have the content read out loud at the same time.
+
+[Learn more about Read & Speak settings](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/#modal-vision_read-speak-settings)
-Customize colors, text size, transparency, contrast, and more. Students can use Larger Text and Bold Text for simple font adjustments or quickly adjust text size from Control Center. Invert display colors and utilize Color Filters to improve contrast. To tone down bright colors, use Reduce White Point. Enable Reduce Transparency for solid backgrounds, and use Increase Contrast to increase foreground/background distinction. Settings can be assigned globally or on a per-app basis.
-
-#### VoiceOver
-
-VoiceOver describes what's onscreen—audibly, in braille, or both—enabling easy navigation via gestures, trackpad, keyboard, or a refreshable braille display. Students can type in braille directly on the touchscreen with Braille Screen Input and get descriptions of objects in the real world, such as people, doors, text, and furniture in indoor spaces with Live Recognition. 6 VoiceOver also offers deep customization options to the built-in voice for speech feedback. 7
-
-#### Braille Access
-
-Braille Access turns a device like iPad or Mac into a full-featured braille notetaker. Easily open any app or Braille Ready Format (BRF) files with a connected braille device and quickly take notes in braille format. Perform calculations using Nemeth Braille or UEB Math, two braille codes often used in classrooms for math and science. And an integrated form of Live Captions lets students and teachers transcribe conversations in real time directly on braille displays. 2
-
-#### Share accessibility settings
-
-Quickly and temporarily share accessibility settings with another iPad while in the classroom. Easily toggle on features that support visual accommodations, like Increase Contrast or Reduce Motion. Or share Touch Accommodations to support a student's unique taps and touches on another device.
+Display settings and text size tools enlarge content and optimize contrast so students with low vision can read textbooks, notes, and assignments without eye strain. Students can adjust text size with Larger Text or add weight with Bold Text. They can also invert colors for a dark background that helps text stand out, add Color Filters for vision deficiencies, tone down bright displays with Reduce White Point, enhance foreground-background contrast with Increase Contrast, or make backgrounds solid using Reduce Transparency. These settings can be assigned globally or per-app, ensuring a student's preferences follow them across every subject.
+
+[Learn more about Display & Text Size](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/#modal-vision_display-settings-text-size)
+
+#### Zoom
+
+Zoom is a screen magnifier that enlarges the content on a device to enhance readability. Learners can choose Full Screen Zoom to magnify the entire screen or Window Zoom to magnify only a portion of the screen with a resizable lens and apply filters such as Inverted, Grayscale, Grayscale Inverted, or Low Light to the magnified area. 6 Students can track text selections, the text insertion point, and typing with Follow Focus. Smart Typing magnifies the text area while keeping the keyboard unmagnified during typing, so students can see what they’re writing without losing their place.
+
+[Learn more about Zoom](https://www.apple.com/accessibility/features/#modal-vision_zoom)
-Hover Text makes it easier to view text on iPad or Mac. If a paragraph, caption, or footnote is too small to read, hover over it and press the activation key for a bigger, higher‑resolution version. Hover Color on Mac helps students who are color blind or have low vision decipher the color beneath their cursor by translating color pixels into simple-to-understand color names. With Hover Typing, students can display larger text when typing in a text field—in a customized font and text color.

item.title: [UPDATED] iPhone Mirroring: Use your iPhone from your Mac
item.description:
With iPhone Mirroring, you can wirelessly interact with your iPhone and its apps and notifications from your Mac. Your iPhone stays locked, so no one else can access it or use it to see what you’re doing.

0 added · 156 removed

-- [iPhone Mirroring system requirements](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#requirements)
-
-- [Start or stop iPhone Mirroring](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#start)
-
-- [Interact with iPhone using iPhone Mirroring](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#interact)
-
-- [Move or resize the iPhone Mirroring window](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#move-or-resize)
-
-- [Manage iPhone notifications](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#notifications)
-
-- [Copy items between devices](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#copy)
-
-- [Change iPhone Mirroring settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#settings)
-
-- [If you need help](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#help)
-
-## iPhone Mirroring system requirements
-
-iPhone Mirroring can be used with only one Mac and one iPhone at a time. Your devices must meet these requirements:
-
-- Your Mac is using macOS Sequoia 15 or later and is a [Mac with Apple silicon](https://support.apple.com/en-us/116943) or [Mac with the Apple T2 Security Chip](https://support.apple.com/en-us/103265) . Live Activities on Mac requires macOS Tahoe 26 or later.
-
-- Your iPhone is using iOS 18 or later and is [set up to use a passcode](https://support.apple.com/en-us/119586) .
-
-- Your iPhone and Mac are [signed in to the same Apple Account](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111001) using [two-factor authentication](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102660) .
-
-- Your iPhone and Mac have Bluetooth and Wi-Fi turned on.
-
-- Your iPhone is locked and near your Mac. It can also be charging and [using StandBy](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/iph878d77632/ios) .
-
-- Your Mac is not [sharing its internet connection](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchlp1540/mac) or using [AirPlay](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchld7e543a0/mac) or [Sidecar](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102597) .
-
-iPhone Mirroring is currently unavailable in the European Union. To simply view but not interact with your iPhone screen or its streamed video on an AirPlay-compatible device, you can [use AirPlay](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102661) instead.
-
-## Start or stop iPhone Mirroring
-
-- On your Mac, click iPhone Mirroring in the Dock. Or open it from the Applications folder or Spotlight or Siri AI . It's included with macOS Sequoia 15 or later.
-
-- If your Mac asks you to unlock your iPhone, use your iPhone to enter your iPhone passcode.
-
-- If your Mac asks whether to allow notifications from your iPhone, click Allow or Don’t Allow. You can change this later in [Notifications settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#notifications) on your Mac.
-
-- If your Mac asks whether to require Mac login to access your iPhone, choose whether to be asked every time or to authenticate automatically. You can change this later in [iPhone Mirroring settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#settings) .
-
-- When iPhone Mirroring shows your iPhone screen, it’s connected to your iPhone and you can use it to interact with your iPhone. [Can’t connect to your iPhone?](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#help)
-
-- To stop mirroring your iPhone, quit the iPhone Mirroring app or unlock your iPhone.
-
-If you have more than one iPhone signed in to your Apple Account and nearby, you can [choose the iPhone that your Mac uses](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#choose-iphone) for mirroring and iPhone notifications.
-
-
-Privacy & Security: iPhone Mirroring automatically pauses the connection after periods of inactivity. While mirroring, your iPhone says that it's in use and identifies the Mac using it. When unlocked after mirroring, it says that it was used from a Mac and links to Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity > iPhone Mirroring, which identifies the Mac that used your iPhone, including when and for how long.
-
-## Interact with iPhone using iPhone Mirroring
-
-Tap, swipe, and type | Use your Mac mouse or trackpad to click wherever you would tap on your iPhone. Or click and hold wherever you would touch and hold, such as to edit the Home Screen or open a quick actions menu . You can scroll or swipe with your mouse or trackpad, and use your Mac keyboard to type and use keyboard shortcuts. To swipe left or right, you can also press and hold the Shift key while scrolling. To use a wireless game controller with iPhone apps that support it, use Bluetooth to connect the controller to your iPhone instead of your Mac.
-
-Go to the Home Screen | Move the pointer to the top of the iPhone Mirroring window, then click the Home Screen button in the toolbar. Or click the bar at the bottom of the iPhone Mirroring window. Or press Command-1 on your keyboard.
-
-Open the App Switcher | Move the pointer to the top of the iPhone Mirroring window, then click the App Switcher button in the toolbar. Or press Command-2 on your keyboard.
-
-Open Spotlight | Use your mouse or trackpad to scroll or swipe up from the Home Screen. Or press Command-3 on your keyboard.
-
-Open Control Center | Press Command-4 on your keyboard. (Requires macOS 27 or later.)
-
-Play audio or video | iPhone audio plays through your Mac, and your Mac controls the volume, unless you're listening through headphones connected to your iPhone. iPhone video plays back in the iPhone Mirroring window. Streaming content providers might have playback restriction policies that affect whether their premium video content can be mirrored.
-
-Access to the iPhone camera and mic is not available in iPhone Mirroring, including for Face ID or phone calls. You can [make and receive phone calls on your Mac](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102405) instead. To make calls from your Mac while iPhone Mirroring is in use, both devices must have [Wi-Fi Calling turned on](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108066) .
-
-## Move or resize the iPhone Mirroring window
-
-To change the position of the iPhone Mirroring window, move the pointer to the top of the window, then drag the window by the toolbar that appears.
-
-To change the size of the iPhone Mirroring window:
-
-- Use the View menu in the menu bar to choose from three preset sizes: Larger, Smaller, or Actual Size. Or press Command–Plus sign (+), Command–Minus sign (–), or Command-0 to switch between sizes.
-
-- In macOS 27 or later, you can drag a corner of the iPhone Mirroring window to resize it. Some apps, such as Mail, Messages, and Calendar, are designed to show more information when you drag to make the window wider. You can then return to standard iPhone size by clicking the iPhone size button in the iPhone Mirroring toolbar, or by pressing Command-9.
-
-iPhone Mirroring automatically switches to and from landscape view as required by the app that you’re using.

item.title: [UPDATED] What to expect during account recovery
item.description:
Account recovery helps you regain access to your Apple Account when you can’t reset your password. Learn what to expect during the wait, how to check your status, and the few things to do (and not to do) while you wait. Apple Support can't shorten the wait period.

-# How to use account recovery when you can’t reset your Apple Account password
+# What to expect during account recovery
-If you use two-factor authentication and can’t sign in or reset your password, you can regain access after an account recovery waiting period.
+Account recovery helps you regain access to your Apple Account when you can’t reset your password. Learn what to expect during the wait, how to check your status, and the few things to do (and not to do) while you wait. Apple Support can't shorten the wait period.
-## What is account recovery?
+If you haven't started account recovery, first try to change or reset your password to regain access to your account. [Learn how...](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102656)
-The account recovery process helps you reset your password and regain access to your account. If you can’t remember your Apple Account password, make sure you’ve tried everything else before starting account recovery – for example, using a different device that’s already signed in to change your password.
+## What to expect
-For security reasons, it might take several days or longer before you can use your account again after you start account recovery. Contacting Apple Support can’t help you shorten this time. This delay is inconvenient, but it’s important so that Apple can keep your account and information safe.
+- Confirmation email — You’ll receive a confirmation email (or iMessage for accounts that use only a phone number) with the specific date and time that you can expect to regain access to your Apple Account. This email arrives within 72 hours after you start account recovery.
-## Before starting account recovery
+- Wait period — For your security, account recovery might take several days or longer. This delay is inconvenient, but it’s important so that Apple can keep your account and information safe. Contacting Apple Support can’t help shorten the wait.
-Try other methods to access your account before starting account recovery.

-- If you haven’t already, try to [reset your password](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102656) on a trusted device.

+A few things will interrupt or cancel your recovery request.
-- If you don’t have a device that you can use, you can [reset your password using the Apple Support app](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102656#supportapp) on a family member’s iPhone or iPad. You can also visit an Apple Store and ask to use a device.

+- Don't submit another request . Unless you find additional recovery factors, submitting another won't speed up the process and might extend the wait.
